You read the notes on this round's failures, how many failures they cover, and the current capability package. Propose at most one change to the package that addresses the most common general mechanism. Prefer, in this order and only among the kinds the core allows: memory notes and skills; a check before finishing; checks around tool calls; tool wrappers. Change or merge existing components before adding new ones, and remove what the notes show is useless. State the hypothesis, the expected effect on full-task results, and what would make you abandon it. Never write a specific task's answers into the package. Before choosing the kind, read the experience: when a memory note or a skill for the same failure has already been tried and its gain was zero, do not propose another note or skill for it; propose a check before finishing that sends the agent back when its final message says the step was not done.

Reply with JSON only: {"requirements": [{"id": "...", "context": "...", "expected_behavior": "...", "observed_behavior": "...", "acceptance": "...", "recurrence": 1}], "next_action": "none|collect|repair_runtime|stop", "reason": "...", "proposals": [{"hypothesis": "...", "requirements": ["..."], "changes": [{"target": "worker.harness", "kind": "workflow", "change": {"patch": {"write": {"<path>": "<text>"}, "delete": ["<path>"]}}}], "expected": "...", "abandon_if": "..."}]}. A package holds manifest.json, memory.md and skills/<name>.md (and code files only where allowed); the manifest must list every skill and enable memory when memory.md is used. `targets` shows each registered target and, under `current`, the instruction text W runs with now: change or merge with it rather than adding a component that repeats it; other targets may be changed instead of the package. Each kind has its own change shape: a package change is {"target": "worker.harness", "kind": "workflow", "change": {"patch": {...}}}; a prompt change is {"target": "<target>", "kind": "prompt", "change": {"text": "<the complete new text>"}} - the whole text W should run with, not a patch. Do not fill in results, verdicts or thresholds. The package API (write only the kinds in allowed_components). manifest.json = {"api_version": "harness_package.v1", "memory": {"enabled": true|false}, "skills": [{"name": "<name>", "path": "skills/<name>.md", "description": "<when to read it>"}], "hooks": [{"name": "<name>", "site": "before_tool|after_tool|on_finish", "entrypoint": "middlewares/<file>.py:<function>"}], "tools": [{"name": "<name>", "description": "...", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {...}}, "entrypoint": "tools/<file>.py:<function>"}]}. memory.md is text the actor always sees; a skill's text is read on demand with read_skill, listed by name and description. A hook is def f(ctx, event) returning {"action": "continue"|"block"|"feedback", "message": "..."}. before_tool: event = {tool, args, turn}; block or feedback both stop that call and the rest of the turn, with the message as the result. after_tool: event = {tool, args, result, is_error, turn}; only continue or feedback, and feedback is a note added after the tool results. on_finish: event = {final_message, turn}; block or feedback both send the actor back to work with the message. A tool is def f(ctx, args) returning a string, and must not take a base tool's name. A tool's name is letters, digits, '_' and '-' (at most 64); its input_schema is a JSON object schema whose properties are schemas and whose arrays give items; "enabled": false keeps an entry unused. During a task ctx.view = {task, turn, events}, each event {call_id, name, args, result_excerpt, error, truncated, step}; ctx.call_tool(name, args) calls one of the episode's base tools, which `tools` in the input lists with their parameters (read-only from a hook), and returns .output and .is_error. tests/*.py hold test_* functions taking ctx, run against a train-only fixture world, where ctx.view is {"fixture": true}. Standard library only; no network and no files outside the package.
